newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - EBRD SAYS EYES STAKES IN STATE BANKS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - EBRD SAYS EYES STAKES IN STATE BANKS.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is looking cautiously at buying into Lithuania's state banks, an official said on Wednesday.
"In the banking sector, we are looking at several of the banks which are on the list for privatisation," said EBRD Deputy Vice President Guy de Selliers.
"Realistically, there are only two: just the State Commercial Bank and the Agricultural Bank," de Selliers said.
"We are not saying we will participate. It's a question of the existing owner, the government...and it's an issue of the EBRD being satisfied with these as good investments," de Sellier said.
The EBRD is an equity investor in Hermis Bank and the Lithuanian Development Bank.
De Sellier said the EBRD supported the government's plans for privatising the banks and would continue to work with existing private banks.
"There is no question that the banking sector is the corner stone of the economy," de Selliers said.
The Lithuanian State Commercial Bank is expected to be the first of the three state banks sold off. The Agricultural Bank is expected to come second, followed at some point by the Savings Bank.
"It's too far away, but the Savings Bank is clearly interesting," de Selliers said.
